messages:
carla-support: heads-up — tenant 'omega-inc' (t-0xA9) opened a support ticket: p95 token latency spiked from ~2.3s -> ~12s on Dedicated eu-west-2 pool (pool-7) and intermittent 429s. Customer also called out a billing jump in the same window. alert: https://console.redwood/alerts/ALRT-789

carla-support: paste from their curl: ```
POST /v1/generate 200ms
...
{"request_id":"r-33","status":429,"error":"Too Many Requests"}
{"request_id":"r-34","latency_ms":12345}
```

alice-eng: thanks. can you confirm pool id / MIG config? any recent rollout?

carla-support: pool=dedicated-eu-west-2-pool-7, MIG layout as reported by provisioning: 3x 1g.20gb slices per host (weird, customer claims they saw 1g+shared), no platform rollout in the window in prod. attaching customer's tenant id and sample request headers (they're using batching size 8).

bob-sre: I'll grab node-side metrics. early hypothesis: noisy-sibling causing SM saturation + token-level throttling from our rate shaper. asking ops to check GPU slice contention and SM utilization. can someone run quick checks on one of the hosts serving pool-7?

alice-eng: @bob-sre which checks? I've got SSH to the host that served the example request: host-7e2a. planning to run nvidia and perf sampling.

bob-sre: run these: ```
# check MIG and GPU mem usage
nvidia-smi -L
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,utilization.gpu --format=csv
# for MIG slice details (NVIDIA tools)
/opt/nvidia/bin/migctl list --format json
```
please paste outputs. also capture dmesg for any GPU driver errors.

alice-eng: pasted outputs: ```
GPU 0: A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-xxxx)
memory.total [MiB], memory.used [MiB], utilization.gpu [%]
81920, 73240, 95
81920, 1280, 4
--- MIG list ---
[MIG instance 0: 1g.20gb, MIG instance 1: 1g.20gb, MIG instance 2: 1g.20gb]
```

mike-ml: interesting — one slice at 95% util and two idle suggests co-residency skew. KV-cache miss rate for tenant during spike? any cache-eviction logs?

alice-eng: grabbed runtime metrics from the pod: KV_CACHE_MISS_RATE=0.78 at spike, batch queue length spiked to 34, p95 model compute jumped accordingly.

eva-eng: customer mentioned "auth errors" — do logs show 401s? or were they mixing 429 + billing anomalies?

carla-support: their support transcript included an expired-token line earlier but all errors in our request logs are 429/timeouts, not 401. billing-bot shows some huge token counts around the spike window for tenant t-0xA9 — looks correlated with retry storms.

billing-bot: auto-note — billing anomaly detected for t-0xA9: +7200% tokens in 15m window vs baseline. flagged for manual review.

bob-sre: retry storms make sense if clients backoff incorrectly. but the underlying cause is likely GPU slice saturation causing high latencies so clients retried. we should confirm whether autoscaler tried to add more capacity and failed or if us throttling kicked in. check autoscale events: ```kubectl get hpa -n dedicated-pool-7```

alice-eng: autoscaler events: scaled from 12 -> 12 (throttle due to quota), there is an autoscale-block event referencing quota-per-tenant limit. logs attached.

mike-ml: TLDR: noisy neighbor (one tenant or batch job) saturated an MIG slice -> backend latency -> client retries -> apparent billing spike + 429s from global rate limiter. Could be mispacked jobs on same host causing hotspot.

tom-customer: confirming from our side: we run a nightly batch at 23:35 UTC (size 8, rolling concurrency 10) — we didn't change code. only started seeing errors yesterday. we haven't received any 401s. happy to share request IDs.

alice-eng: can customer provide a short repro (small script that reproduces batch pattern) and a list of request_ids from the affected window? if we can repro on a mirrored host we can validate scheduling/pack policy.

carla-support: tom, can you share 3 request_ids and the exact headers/backoff behavior? we will set up a debug session.

infra-bot: [alert] Dedicated pool 7: MIG slice GPU util >90% for 6m. Created incident INC-2026-0432.

bob-sre: next troubleshooting steps for infra team: 1) pin a test instance of tenant to an isolated MIG slice and reproduce batch workload 2) run perf sampling to validate SM saturation vs memory bandwidth 3) check scheduler packing heuristics (we may be packing a heavy batch job with another heavy tenant) 4) validate autoscaler quotas and immediate fallback behavior 5) confirm rate limiter response codes map to throttle policy not auth.

mike-ml: also check KV cache eviction tuning — high miss rate indicates we're warming repeatedly which amplifies GPU work. consider a temporary increase to per-tenant cache size for repro window.

eva-eng: I'll prepare a canary config to pin tenant to its own slice for 30m and watch billing + latency. need approval from product infra - looping in owners in a follow-up thread.

carla-support: created a short-term mitigation: moved some of customer traffic to a dedicated reserved slice for 1h and asked them to run their nightly batch now. asked them to avoid aggressive retries.

tom-customer: running now. will report back in 15m.

alice-eng: recording actions for postmortem: - cause: noisy neighbor / MIG slice skew leading to SM saturation - immediate mitigation: temporary slice isolation, throttle tuning - follow-ups: scheduler packing fix, autoscale quota review, KV-cache tuning, billing audit for retry storms

carla-support: thanks all. if tom confirms improvement we'll keep isolation for 1 hour then revert and run controlled repro. will open dedicated-ticket to product infra for scheduler/policy changes. :thumbsup:
